## Intensity distribution

<img class="chart chart--light" src="/images/measured/2026-08/zones.png" alt="Heart-rate zones" loading="lazy" decoding="async" /><img class="chart chart--dark" src="/images/measured/2026-08/zones-dark.png" alt="Heart-rate zones" loading="lazy" decoding="async" />

99% of recorded heart-rate time was in Z1–Z2 and 0.1% in Z4–Z5.

> ⚠️ **Data check:** almost no time above Z2 usually means the zones are set too high, not that the training was all easy. Zones hang off an *auto-estimated* LTHR of 178 bpm (max HR 192). A proper threshold test would make this chart trustworthy.

<details>
<summary>How these numbers are made</summary>

- Source: 15 activities from Strava/Garmin FIT files, processed by my self-hosted [performance-lab](/project). Last activity included: 2026-08-29.
- **Load** uses the TSS scale (100 = one hour at threshold), integrated second by second from heart rate, so a winter of treadmill runs doesn't look like a loss of fitness.
- **CTL/ATL** are 42- and 7-day exponentially weighted load; **TSB** = yesterday's CTL − ATL.
- **VO2max** combines Daniels' oxygen-cost equation with Swain's %HRmax→%VO2max relation, per steady outdoor run ≥ 20 min. It is scaled by ×0.868 so the 12-month median matches the VDOT of my half-marathon PB (1:30:37).
- Sessions flagged implausible (e.g. a 50-hour swim from a manual-entry typo) are excluded.
</details>
